title: The Doppler factor
spoken: The frequency ratio is gamma times one minus v over c times the unprimed direction cosine.
explanation: How the frequency changes depends on the speed and on the light's direction. At v = 0.6c, light travelling along the motion (phi = 0) gives q = 0.5; light across it (phi = 90 degrees) gives q = 1.25.
assumptions: The moving system moves along x at speed v relative to the stationary system, with |v| < c. Modern teaching notation: gamma is the paper's beta, c its V.
A plane light wave whose direction makes the angle phi with the direction of motion, in the stationary system.
The same wave phase, written in both systems' coordinates, fixes frequency and direction together.

notes.title: One minus that
notes.explanation: Below 1 for light along the motion, 1 for light across it.

notes.title: Cosine of the angle
notes.explanation: 1 for light along the motion, 0 for light across it, −1 for light against it.

notes.title: How much of the motion is along the light
notes.explanation: v over c times the cosine: zero when the light crosses the motion at right angles.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: The frequency ratio for this light, from the transformation of its phase. Sound gives a similar-looking rule by a different argument; the analogy is not the derivation.

notes.title: Times gamma
notes.explanation: Gamma alone survives for light at right angles: a frequency change with no motion along the light.

notes.title: v over c
notes.explanation: The speed as a fraction of the speed of light.

notes.title: The light's angle, stationary system
notes.explanation: Between the light's direction and the direction of motion, measured in the stationary system. Name the frame: the angle is different in the other one.

notes.title: Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: One over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared. At 0.6c it is 1.25.

notes.title: The frequency ratio
notes.explanation: The moving system's frequency over the stationary system's.

notes.title: Speed of the moving system
notes.explanation: Signed along x: the sign says which way the system moves.

sentence.text: the light's angle to the motion
